newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Petrochem mulls huge China project.
newsitem.headline: China Petrochem mulls huge China project.

text.p: Taiwan's China Petrochemical Development Corp said on Wednesday it was considering a long-term plan to invest T$30 billion to build a nylon fibre plant in China if Taiwan-China relations improve.

"We are considering a long-term plan to invest T$30 billion in China, but the premise is the cross-straits (Taiwan-China) relations must improve," Wang Pai-hsien, China Petrochemical vice-president, told Reuters.

The company plans to build the plant in China's southeastern provinces, hoping to reach an annual production capacity of 300,000 tonnes of nylon fibre when the projct is completed in three stages by 2003, Wang said by telephone.
Each stage would have an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, Wang said.
After completion, the planned new plant will generate an annaul revenue of T$30 billion for China Petrochemical, with expected annual profit of T$4 billion, Wang said.
Taiwan, which has banned direct links with China since a civil war split them in 1949, has allowed a range of "indirect" investments under a political thaw dating to the late 1980s.
Taipei said last week it would allow Taiwan firms to engage in a wider range of investments in arch rival China, while also slapping an outright ban on real estate and large power plant projects.
China Petrochemical was transferred to private hands when its state stake fell to 37 percent from 80 percent in June 1994.
